subject: Expedited GCP private offer — CloudGoods: rev-share carveout + termination clause
messages:
From: Anna Kowalski <anna.k@cloudgoods.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@cloudgoods.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer request — CloudGoods (GCP)

Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed. We're under a procurement deadline with a strategic GCP migration and need a private offer in place by early December to qualify for our board funding window. Two items are blocking internal sign-off:

- Rev-share: we need a stepped rev-share schedule (20% first 12 months, 28% thereafter) to justify the initial discount in our internal model.
- Termination: we require a 90-day termination-for-convenience right after the first 12 months (we're standardizing flexibility across vendors).

Can Redwood accommodate those non-standard terms? If you can provide an updated term sheet and a tentative DocuSign link, procurement will run the approvals next week.

Attachments: CloudGoods_RFP_Appendix.pdf

Anna
Anna Kowalski
Director, Cloud Procurement
CloudGoods

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer request — CloudGoods (GCP)

Folks — looked through the numbers and legal asks. Short summary of impact and recommended guardrails: 

Impact:
- Rev-share: Standard marketplace split is 30% to partner. Moving to 20% for first 12 months reduces ARR-derived revenue by ~46% in year one (model attached).
- Upfront credit: $75k is material relative to expected first-year consumption; requires finance sign-off.
- Termination: Term-for-convenience at 90 days post-12mo creates churn risk — we'd need a minimum usage runout or pro-rated clawback to avoid revenue leakage.

Recommendation for exec approval (narrow carveout):
1) Approve stepped rev-share: 20% for first 12 months, then 28% for months 13–24; this is an exception limited to this deal and requires tracking in Redwood's Partner Incentive registry.
2) Upfront credit capped at $75k, paid as a one-time invoice credit; Finance (Mina) to approve cash-flow terms and recovery if consumption <X.
3) Termination concession only with a pro-rated clawback for unused committed spend (90 days notice triggers pro-rata return of credits, and any unused committed minimums billed immediately).
4) Net-60 acceptable only with credit approval and purchase order; otherwise default to Net-30.

If leadership signs off on the above guardrails I will draft the exception memo for Exec approval and instruct legal to prepare redlines that implement the clawback.

Karthik Iyer
Head, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference

Attachment: RG-2026-0491_revshare_model.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T08:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer request — CloudGoods (GCP)

Appreciate the analysis. I'm OK to recommend exec approval with conditions — CloudGoods is strategically important and the board timeline is real. Conditions I want documented in the exec memo: 

- Exception limited to RG-2026-0491 and invalid for renewals/other deals.
- 20% rev-share floor for months 0–12, 28% months 13–24. Exception auto-expires at month 25 unless expressly renewed by Exec.
- Termination-for-convenience only allowed with the pro-rated clawback Karthik described; clawback calculation to be spelled out in the SOW.
- Upfront credit capped at $75k, recoupable if first 6 months' consumption < 50% of forecast.
- Legal to push the customer to accept a 30-day payment period on any clawback invoices (collectability protection).

Olga: please produce the redline that enforces the clawback and a short describing paragraph for the exec memo. Mina: confirm finance OK with the recip structure on the $75k credit (how we record it and expected cash impact).

I'll sign the memo and escalate to VP Sales / CFO for final sign-off.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private offer request — CloudGoods (GCP) — Exec memo and redlines attached

Team — attached the redline and exec memo draft. Highlights of the legal changes I added: 

- Section 6.2 (Marketplace Revenue Share) — clarifies the stepped schedule and includes a record-keeping covenant for the partner to verify consumption.
- New Section 9.4 (Termination and Clawback) — if Customer exercises termination-for-convenience in months 13+, Customer will reimburse pro-rated portion of any upfront credit and any prepaid committed minimums; collection language references netting against outstanding invoices and 30-day payment term for clawbacks.
- Payment terms: preserved Net-30 for any clawback invoices; customer requested Net-60 remains on consumption invoices but clause requires PO and finance approval.

I've attached: CloudGoods_SOW_redline.docx and the Exec_Approval_Memo_RG-2026-0491.pdf.

If Marissa signs the memo I'll route to VP Sales and then the CFO for final signature. Recommend Serg to provide the DocuSign link to the customer once exec signs.

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
